fixed_ritz_setup.onsite_space: Fix one complete parity-preserving onsite spectral-cluster Ritz label M with dimension d_M independent of N. For all sufficiently large N, the retained onsite space has rank d_M, contains the exact even/odd doublet, and the compressed onsite energy has norm at most D_M N^2.
fixed_ritz_setup.classical_reference: On each forward star use h_(x,N)^0=sum_(i=1)^3[(k_x+k_(x+e_i))/6+J_N(1-s_x s_(x+e_i))]. In the tensor product spectral basis this is a classical finite-range m-potential with exactly the all-plus and all-minus periodic zero-energy configurations.
fixed_ritz_setup.spectral_data: For large N, 1<=J_N<=J_M^* because J_N tends to 8, Gamma_N>=c_Gamma,M N^2, and the exact local star gap is min{2J_N,Gamma_N/6+J_N}. On each positive edge the residual obeys |V_(e,N)(psi,psi)|<=alpha_N h_(e,N)^0(psi,psi)+beta_N ||psi||^2 with alpha_N<=C_alpha,M N^-2 and beta_N<=C_beta,M N^-3; grouping three positive edges changes only the additive term to 3 beta_N.
fixed_ritz_setup.source: Add the bounded parity-odd parameter h sum_x s_(x,N), allocated over the fixed-range interaction. Its all-plus/all-minus energy-density derivatives differ by two, and the residual is h-independent.

peierls_charging.sampling: Choose a fixed sampling cube W_a larger than the star range and the period one reference patterns. A defective cube contains either a high site or two opposite low labels; in the latter case a nearest-neighbour path contains a disagreeing low edge.
peierls_charging.bounded_overlap: There is a finite geometric constant C_a such that the number S of defective sampling cubes is at most C_a(L+H), and the number S_high of high-defect cubes is at most C_a H, where L is the number of disagreeing low edges and H the number of high sites.
peierls_charging.energy: The classical energy is at least 2J_N L+Gamma_N H. For J_N>=1 and Gamma_N>1, kappa_M=1/(2C_a) and D_(M,N)=(Gamma_N-1)/(2C_a) give E(gamma)>kappa_M S(gamma)+D_(M,N) S_high(gamma). Thus kappa_M>0 is N-independent and D_(M,N)>=c_M Gamma_N-C'_M is of order N^2.
peierls_charging.boundary: No claim kappa_M=1 or D_(M,N)=Gamma_N/6 is made. The constants depend on the fixed sampling geometry and M only through the declared fixed data.

dffr_block_reduction.factorization: On each positive edge put B_(e,N)=alpha_N h_(e,N)^0+beta_N I. The two-sided form bound and finite dimension give V_(e,N)=B_(e,N)^(1/2) C_(e,N) B_(e,N)^(1/2) with a selfadjoint contraction C_(e,N).
dffr_block_reduction.projections: Let P_X^0 be the tensor product of the onsite doublet projectors on the two-site edge support, and Q_X^0=I-P_X^0. Both commute with B_(e,N).
dffr_block_reduction.operator_blocks: The fixed-M energy ceiling and the O(1) low-reference spectrum give ||P phi P||=O_M(N^-2), ||Q phi Q||=O_M(1), and ||Q phi P||+||P phi Q||=O_M(N^-1).
dffr_block_reduction.hilbert_schmidt: DFFR uses Hilbert-Schmidt interaction bounds. On a two-site edge, the safe DFFR equation (4.10) estimate ||T||_HS<=d_M^2||T|| converts the three operator estimates with one N-independent factor.
dffr_block_reduction.lambda_convention: The lambda in DFFR (5.21)-(5.22) is an exponential-support bookkeeping parameter, not the physical interpolation endpoint. Fix lambda_0=1/2 and define the auxiliary family Q_(X,N)(lambda)=(lambda/lambda_0)^(s(X)) V_(X,N), so Q_N(lambda_0)=V_N is exactly the physical t=1 residual. Since an edge has s(X)=2, equation (5.21) holds throughout the auxiliary family with epsilon_(alpha,delta,N)=lambda_0^(-2)||V_(alpha,delta,N)||_HS=4||V_(alpha,delta,N)||_HS; the source derivative is zero.
dffr_block_reduction.criterion: DFFR Theorem 5.2 requires the maximum of exp(-beta kappa_bar), lambda epsilon_ll/kappa, lambda sqrt(epsilon_lh epsilon_hl/[kappa(kappa+D)]), lambda epsilon_hh/(kappa+D), lambda epsilon_hl/(kappa+D), and lambda epsilon_lh/(kappa+D) to be below epsilon_0. The five nonthermal terms are respectively O(N^-2), O(N^-2), O(N^-2), O(N^-3), and O(N^-3).
dffr_block_reduction.uniformity: For fixed d_M, fixed range, two reference patterns, fixed kappa_M, and lambda_0, the contour combinatorics and threshold epsilon_0 are N-independent; D_(M,N) is retained explicitly and only improves the high-sector denominators. Hence there are N_M and beta_M such that the physical residual enters for N>=N_M and beta>=beta_M.

phase_conclusion.regular_diagram: DFFR Theorem 5.2 yields a regular smooth deformation of the two-pattern zero-temperature diagram and two stable low-temperature phases at its maximal-coexistence point.
phase_conclusion.zero_source_pin: Parity sends h to -h, exchanges the two reference patterns and the two stable phases, and leaves the residual invariant. Uniqueness of the regular maximal-coexistence point therefore pins it exactly to h=0.
phase_conclusion.order: Define q_(M,N,beta) as the maximum of the six DFFR (5.22) entries, or the fixed monotone contour majorant used in that proof; it tends to zero as N and beta grow at fixed M. DFF I Theorem 2.2 and equation (2.81), as invoked by DFFR II, make the stable expectations of the bounded Ritz sign s_(x,N) differ from the plus/minus reference values by O(q_(M,N,beta)). Existentially enlarge N_M and beta_M until this error is below the chosen one-quarter target; the two expectations then have opposite nonzero signs and are distinct.
phase_conclusion.ground_limits: For each fixed M and each sufficiently large fixed N, beta-to-infinity cluster limits of the two stable phases are distinct ordered ground states of the same fixed-Ritz zero-source Hamiltonian.
phase_conclusion.scope: The conclusion is fixed M and large N. It is not uniform in M and supplies no Ritz removal, full-oscillator phase theorem, common spatial algebra, common-alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS quotient, GNS implementation or spectral gap.

Convergent Perturbation Expansions and Stability in Systems with Infinite Degeneracy, Helvetica Physica Acta 69 (1996), 752-820, Theorem 5.2 and equations (5.21)-(5.22).
literature_scope.dff_1996_ground_limit: N. Datta, R. Fernandez and J. Frohlich, Low-temperature phase diagrams of quantum lattice systems. I. Stability for quantum perturbations of classical systems with finitely-many ground states, Journal of Statistical Physics 84 (1996), 455-534, Theorem 2.2 and equation (2.81), as invoked by DFFR II for convergence of stable phase expectations to ground-state expectations as beta tends to infinity.
literature_scope.yarotskii_boundary: D. A. Yarotskii, Pirogov-Sinai theory for relatively bounded quantum perturbations of classical lattice models, Russian Math. Surveys 61:2 (2006), 371-372, gives only an existential small neighbourhood for each finite-dimensional model. The present fixed-M proof instead verifies the explicit DFFR two-level criterion and does not infer a common radius from pointwise radii.
